stem: A client with fever and productive cough has neutrophilia with increased immature neutrophil forms. Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: The pattern is compatible with acute infection or inflammation; in this clinical setting, bacterial respiratory infection is an important concern that requires correlation with other findings.
options.B: The pattern favors an uncomplicated viral illness and makes bacterial infection less likely despite the fever, productive cough, and immature neutrophil forms.
options.C: The pattern primarily indicates iron-deficiency anemia because neutrophil maturation changes are not associated with acute infectious or inflammatory processes.
options.D: The pattern can be treated as a normal CBC variation, so the respiratory symptoms and other diagnostic findings do not need to be integrated into interpretation.

rationale: StatPearls/NCBI identifies infection and inflammation as the most common causes of secondary neutrophilia and states that bacterial infections are usually associated with a left shift, including increased band forms. It also emphasizes history, examination, CBC/smear review, cultures, and other evaluation to identify the cause. In a client with fever and productive cough, A appropriately raises concern for bacterial respiratory infection while preserving clinical correlation. B misstates the association, C assigns the wrong construct, and D ignores the need for evaluation.
educational_objective: Interpret neutrophilia with immature neutrophil forms as compatible with infection/inflammation and commonly associated with bacterial infection, while integrating the CBC differential with the clinical picture rather than using it as a stand-alone diagnosis.
source_organization: StatPearls / NCBI Bookshelf, National Library of Medicine
source_version_date: StatPearls 2026 edition; article last updated April 27, 2023; live NCBI page retrieved 2026-08-26
source_locator: Etiology > Secondary Neutrophilia > Infection/Inflammation: infection/inflammation are the most common causes; bacterial infections are usually associated with left shift/increased band forms. Evaluation: review CBC/differential, smear, clinical history/examination and targeted testing.
source_claim_supported: Neutrophilia with immature forms is compatible with infection/inflammation and often accompanies bacterial infection but requires clinical correlation.
blueprint_locator: Reduction of Risk Potential — interpret laboratory/diagnostic findings and recognize changes requiring follow-up.
correction_summary: Removed distractor-only absolute wording and kept all alternatives within CBC-differential interpretation.

audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: PASS — left shift supports bacterial infection but is not diagnostic; A preserves that distinction and no other option does.
